punchline: A Stoic tennis player decides before the first serve that winning is not the goal.
thirty_sec: William Irvine sorts life into things you control fully, not at all, or partly. A tennis match is partly, since winning depends on your opponent too. So the Stoic aims to play his best instead of winning, which keeps his mood off the scoreboard. A novelist, likewise, should aim to write well rather than only to get published.
